Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.displayserver.nativewindow.x11

Class CompositedWindowPipeline

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.displayserver.nativewindow.x11.CompositedWindowPipeline
All Implemented Interfaces:
X11Compositor.DamageListener
public final class CompositedWindowPipeline extends Object implements X11Compositor.DamageListener
Wires one WindowPixelSource to one CompositedWindowSink: on a damage report it reads the damaged region and presents it to the sink.

This is the presentation-agnostic spine of the compositor. It implements X11Compositor.DamageListener so it can be registered directly with X11Compositor.addDamageListener(int, X11Compositor.DamageListener) for a window, and it holds no gnu.x11.Display and no Java 3D reference, so the whole dispatch/clamping/lifecycle decision is unit-testable headlessly with a fake source and a fake sink. The 3D desktop registers a texture sink; the 2D desktop registers a Swing sink — the same pipeline drives both.

Threading

damageReported(int, int, int, int, int) runs on the window-manager event thread (the thread the X11Compositor dispatches on), which is the thread that may safely perform the source's synchronous X read. A sink that must update a Swing component marshals to the EDT itself inside CompositedWindowSink.present(java.awt.image.BufferedImage, int, int, int, int).

  • Constructor Details

    • CompositedWindowPipeline

      public CompositedWindowPipeline(WindowPixelSource source, CompositedWindowSink sink)
      Creates a pipeline bound to one window's source and sink, presenting each damage report synchronously (an always-due FramePacer). The windowId carried by each damage event is not re-checked here: a pipeline is registered per window, and its source is already bound to that window.
      Parameters:
      source - reads the window's redirected pixels; never null
      sink - presents them; never null
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if either argument is null

    • CompositedWindowPipeline

      public CompositedWindowPipeline(WindowPixelSource source, CompositedWindowSink sink, FramePacer pacer)
      Creates a pipeline that coalesces damage and paces presents. Damage reports accumulate into a single bounding region (DamageAccumulator); a present happens only when pacer says one is due, otherwise the damage waits for the next due report or an explicit flush(int). An always-due pacer (interval 0) makes this behave exactly like the two-argument constructor.
      Parameters:
      source - reads the window's redirected pixels; never null
      sink - presents them; never null
      pacer - throttles presents; null defaults to always-due
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if source or sink is null

  • Method Details

    • damageReported

      public void damageReported(int windowId, int x, int y, int width, int height)
      Accumulates the damaged region and, when a present is due, reads the coalesced bounding region once and presents it. Negative origins are clamped to zero and empty regions ignored (matching the tile loader's behaviour); a failed read is a silent no-op, since the next damage event retries. With the default always-due pacer this presents each damage report immediately, exactly as before coalescing was added.
      Specified by:
      damageReported in interface X11Compositor.DamageListener
      Parameters:
      windowId - the damaged window
      x - damaged region left, in window pixels
      y - damaged region top, in window pixels
      width - damaged region width
      height - damaged region height

    • flush

      public void flush(int windowId)
      Presents any damage accumulated since the last present, ignoring pacing. A live frame loop calls this once per rendered frame so paced-out damage is not dropped; it is a no-op when nothing is pending.
      Parameters:
      windowId - the X window id (for diagnostics only)
